s1.quote: At a depth of 16 ft (4.9 m), the wreck is in shallow waters, making it suitable for divers of all skill levels.

s2.quote: located between Basswood Island and the Bayfield Peninsula

summary.text: A burned tug lying in very shallow water in the Apostle Islands off Red Cliff, between Basswood Island and the Bayfield Peninsula. Little remains beyond the bottom and scattered machinery, so it suits any diver and is a good easy Lake Superior wreck.

s1.publisher: National Park Service, Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
s1.quote: Visibility normally ranges from 10 to 80 feet, but can be reduced to zero under certain weather conditions.

s2.quote: The burned wreckage remains at the bottom of Julian Bay off Stockton Island.

summary.text: The scattered, burned remains of a schooner-barge rest in the shallows of Julian Bay on Stockton Island in the Apostle Islands. A park dive permit is needed, and visibility swings with weather.

s1.quote: lies in about 54 feet of water off of Outer Island, Lake Superior, in Ashland County … retain excellent integrity … a hard bottom of sandstone bedrock at a maximum depth of 54 feet

s2.quote: cold water, occasional strong surge, and variable visibility

highlights.text: Bilge, port and starboard hull sections intact

summary.text: A huge wooden schooner-barge lost in a 1905 gale, now broken but with its bilge and both sides still well preserved on bedrock off Outer Island. Remote and boat-only, with cold water and variable conditions.

s2.quote: The City of Bangor wreck site is now part of the Keweenaw Underwater Preserve, established in 1991

summary.text: The remains of a freighter that carried new Chrysler cars and ran ashore near Keweenaw Point in 1926 lie in shallow water, part of the Keweenaw Underwater Preserve. Only limited wreckage survives.

s1.quote: She went down with a cargo of farm equipment. Much of the cargo can still be found at this site just off the Harbor House Restaurant.

highlights.text: Farm equipment cargo still on site

s1.quote: The cold waters of the lake have preserved the structure of the ship in 15 to 60 feet (4.6 to 18.3 m) of water.

summary.text: A steel package freighter wrecked on Isle Royale's Glenlyon Shoals in 1924. The cold lake has preserved the bow, engine room and cabin in shallow water, and the open-to-the-public wreck is far less visited than other park wrecks.

s1.quote: The deepest part of the park is 45 feet at high tide … Visibility ranges between two and 40 feet.

s2.quote: Shore access only … Novice … Long swims … It is illegal to dive within 100 yards of the ferry landing

hazards.text: Steel dry dock interferes with compass

access.value: No diving within 100 yards of ferry landing; no night diving without permit

summary.text: A city-run shore-entry underwater park beside the Edmonds ferry dock, with a sunken dry dock, boats and reef structures linked by guide ropes. Popular with newer divers, though visibility varies and swims are long.

s1.quote: The deepest part of the park is 45 feet at high tide … Visibility ranges between two and 40 feet.

s2.quote: Shore access only … Novice … Long swims … It is illegal to dive within 100 yards of the ferry landing

summary.text: The beach access for Edmonds Underwater Park north of the ferry dock; divers swim out to a trail system of sunken vessels and reefs. Suited to novices, with variable visibility and lengthy swims.

s2.quote: waters of 80 to 150 feet (24 to 46 m) … the 120–150 foot depth

highlights.text: Near-perfect steam engine about 20 ft high

summary.text: An 1898 bulk freighter near Rock of Ages Light, Isle Royale, with hull remains in the shallows and a nearly intact steam engine much deeper. Hull pieces mingle with the nearby Cumberland wreck.

s1.quote: Large portions of the ship remain in 20 to 80 feet of water, including the wooden hull, side-wheel, and boiler.

summary.text: A wooden side-wheel passenger steamer lost in 1877 near Rock of Ages Light, Isle Royale. The scattered hull, paddle wheel and boiler lie in modest depth, mixed with debris of the later Henry Chisholm wreck.

s1.quote: under more than 260 feet (79 m) of water

summary.text: A 1927 package freighter resting on its side at the base of an underwater cliff off Kamloops Point, Isle Royale. Well preserved but far below recreational limits, so only for technical divers.
